story.title: Social Security Benefits to Increase by 3.6% in 2027 Amid Rising Inflation
story.summary: Consumer prices rose by 3.7% in September, prompting the Social Security Administration to announce a 3.6% cost-of-living adjustment (COLA) for 2027. This increase, the largest since 2023, will result in an average monthly benefit increase of about $70 for recipients, effective from January 2027.

explore_lenses.label: Why might the raise feel different by recipient?
explore_lenses.title: Average gains do not equal individual gains
explore_lenses.summary: The 3.6% adjustment is applied to each person’s current benefit, so the official $75 figure is an average for retired workers—not a universal payment increase. Its purchasing-power effect will depend on each household’s expenses and other deductions.

claims.text: SSA estimates that the average retired-worker benefit will rise from $2,095 to $2,170 per month in January 2027, a $75 increase; other beneficiary groups have different average dollar increases.
The increase applies to nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries, while about 7.3 million SSI recipients will also receive the 3.6% adjustment.

AARP CEO Myechia Minter-Jordan said the COLA is especially consequential because many older Americans lack retirement savings and report financial insecurity; this is an advocacy perspective, not a measure of what every recipient will experience.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: An individual’s net payment can differ from the gross COLA because benefit amounts, taxes, Medicare premiums and other deductions vary.

explore_lenses.label: How was the 3.6% figure determined?
explore_lenses.title: It follows a statutory CPI-W formula
explore_lenses.summary: September’s 3.7% headline inflation rate helped frame the announcement, but it is not itself the COLA formula. The law bases the adjustment on the change in the average CPI-W for July through September.

claims.text: The Social Security Act’s COLA calculation compares the average CPI-W for the third quarter of 2026 with the third-quarter average from 2025, then rounds the percentage change to the nearest tenth; SSA says that calculation produced 3.6%.

BLS reported that the broader CPI-U rose 3.7% over the 12 months through September 2026, while the CPI-W rose 3.9% over that period; the COLA uses CPI-W and quarterly averages rather than the CPI-U headline figure.
September’s monthly CPI-U increase was driven in large part by gasoline: the gasoline index rose 9.1% during the month, while the all-items index rose 0.6%.

explore_lenses.label: When will payments and notices change?
explore_lenses.title: SSI rises first; Social Security follows in January
explore_lenses.summary: The new amount will not appear immediately for most Social Security recipients. SSI recipients are scheduled to receive the increase at the end of December, and beneficiaries can check their personalized notice before regular January payments begin.

claims.text: The 3.6% Social Security COLA begins with January 2027 benefits; increased SSI payments are scheduled for December 31, 2026 because January 1 is a holiday.
People with a my Social Security account who enroll in digital notices by November 18 can view their COLA notice in late November; SSA says mailed notices will go out during December.
The maximum earnings subject to Social Security payroll tax is set to rise from $184,500 in 2026 to $192,300 in 2027, a separate annual adjustment affecting higher earners.

story_report.summary: Social Security benefits will rise 3.6% in 2027 after consumer prices, as measured by the broader CPI-U, increased 3.7% over the 12 months through September. The adjustment will take effect with January benefits and is expected to add about $70 a month on average, though the actual change will vary by beneficiary. The increase applies to nearly 72 million Social Security beneficiaries, while about 7.3 million Supplemental Security Income recipients will receive the same percentage adjustment.

sections.heading: COLA Formula Uses CPI-W
sections.body: The 3.6% adjustment is based on a formula set by the Social Security Act, which compares the average Consumer Price Index for Urban Wage Earners and Clerical Workers, or CPI-W, for the third quarter of 2026 with the same quarter a year earlier. SSA said that calculation, rounded to the nearest tenth of a percentage point, produced the 3.6% COLA. The CPI-W rose 3.9% over the 12 months through September, compared with 3.7% for the broader CPI-U measure.

sections.heading: Average Retiree Benefit Rises $75
sections.body: SSA estimates the average retired-worker payment will increase from $2,095 to $2,170 a month in January, a $75 gain. Other beneficiary groups will see different average dollar changes. The percentage increase does not necessarily reflect the inflation experienced by a particular older or disabled household, because the statutory CPI-W measure may not match an individual household’s spending pattern.

sections.heading: Notices Detail Individual Payment Changes
sections.body: SSI recipients are scheduled to receive increased payments on Dec. 31, 2026, because Jan. 1 is a holiday. People with my Social Security accounts who sign up for digital notices by Nov. 18 can view their COLA notices in late November; mailed notices are due during December. Separately, the maximum earnings subject to Social Security payroll taxes will increase from $184,500 in 2026 to $192,300 in 2027.

unresolved.text: Each recipient’s exact net payment remains individual: benefit levels, taxes, Medicare premiums and other deductions can cause the amount received to differ from the gross COLA. Recipients must consult their personal notice for their new payment amount.

related_stories.title: Saudi Engineer Charged with Planting Listening Device at OpenAI Offices
related_stories.summary: Abdulrahman Alfozan, a Saudi national and engineer at OpenAI, has been charged by the FBI for allegedly planting a hidden recording device in a conference room at the company's San Francisco office. The device, reportedly wrapped in toilet paper, was discovered inserted into a USB port on the back of a television. Alfozan had been employed at OpenAI since June 2025 before his arrest.

related_stories.title: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis Sentenced to 40 Years to Life for Tupac Shakur's Murder
related_stories.summary: Duane ‘Keffe D’ Davis has been sentenced to 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating the murder of hip-hop artist Tupac Shakur in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas in 1996. Davis was found guilty last month for his role in the crime, which has been a significant event in the history of hip-hop rivalries.

related_stories.title: Federal Judge Blocks Trump's Media Ban on White House Access
related_stories.summary: A federal judge has granted a preliminary injunction that continues to block the Trump administration's attempt to bar CNN, MS Now, and Politico from accessing the White House. This decision is seen as a significant development in the ongoing legal battle between the Trump administration and these media outlets, which has heightened tensions between the White House and journalists.

related_stories.title: Ukraine's Military Faces Starlink Internet Access Restrictions Amid Russian Attacks
related_stories.summary: Ukraine's military has reported sudden restrictions on its access to Starlink satellite internet, which is crucial for its operations. This change coincides with increased Russian missile attacks and a lack of prior warning from the U.S. government. Ukrainian officials have described the impact of these restrictions as severely detrimental, likening it to a nuclear strike against their capabilities.
